title: Add matrix runner for H100/A100 pools + result aggregation (CSV/Parquet) for FP8/INT8 sprint
author: Isabella Rossi
description:
Context: For the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we need a reproducible way to run the full benchmark suite across the fleet GPU pools (H100 + A100) and collect results into a single artifact set that is easy to analyze (Drive + warehouse ingestion). Today we have ad-hoc per-node runs and manual copy/paste into the working sheet, which is slow and makes it easy to lose environment metadata.

This PR adds: (1) a matrix runner that schedules benchmark jobs against named GPU pools (h100/a100) with consistent per-case config, (2) an aggregation step that normalizes per-run JSON artifacts into CSV + Parquet with a stable schema, and (3) a lightweight uploader to the sprint Drive folder. It’s intentionally “boring” glue code so the sprint can move quickly; follow-ups will harden pinning/clock locking (see pr-851) and integrate nsys capture (runtime PR).

Key goals:
- One command to run the matrix for a model/GPU/workload slice (or the whole thing)
- Standardized metadata on every row (git SHA, container tag, CUDA/driver, clocks if locked, model hash, kernel mode, scheduler knobs)
- Warehouse-friendly outputs (Parquet) + analyst-friendly outputs (CSV) + manifest for Drive
- Deterministic case IDs so we can diff baseline vs FP8/INT8 runs and power perf-canary baselines

Usage:
- Dry-run (prints plan, no jobs):
  ./tools/matrix_runner/run_matrix.py --suite top-hosted-v3 --gpus h100,a100 --models llama3-70b,qwen2-72b --workloads prefill_1k_decode_256,mixed_prod --dry-run
- Run with a concurrency cap per pool:
  ./tools/matrix_runner/run_matrix.py --suite top-hosted-v3 --gpus h100,a100 --models @configs/models_top6.txt --workloads @configs/workloads_v3.txt --max-inflight-per-pool 12
- Aggregate a run folder:
  ./tools/matrix_runner/aggregate_results.py --input /mnt/artifacts/runs/2026-02-13T0215Z --out ./out --format csv,parquet
- Upload outputs:
  ./tools/matrix_runner/upload_to_drive.py --run-id 2026-02-13T0215Z --drive-folder-id 1a2b3c... --inputs ./out/results.csv ./out/results.parquet ./out/manifest.jsonl

Schema overview (stable columns):
- run_id, case_id, started_at, completed_at
- repo, git_sha, container_image, cuda_version, driver_version, host_kernel
- gpu_sku, gpu_count, mig_mode, clocks_locked
- suite, model_id, model_revision, quant_mode (baseline|fp8|int8), kernel_profile, scheduler_profile
- workload_id, prompt_len_p50, prompt_len_p95, gen_len, concurrency, batch_size_target
- metrics: ttft_ms_p50/p95, tpot_ms_p50/p95, tokens_per_s, req_per_s, gpu_util_avg, gpu_mem_gb_peak, error_rate
- notes/anomaly tags (free-form)

Implementation notes:
- Runner uses a pool abstraction (configured via YAML) mapping {pool_name -> k8s context/namespace + node selector + resource requests}. This is compatible with our existing benchmark-lab job templates.
- Each benchmark job writes a single artifact directory with: raw.json (per-request samples), summary.json (aggregates), env.json (machine + container), and runner.json (the case config). The aggregator stitches these into a single table.
- Case IDs are generated from a canonical JSON encoding of (suite, model, workload, gpu_sku, quant_mode, kernel_profile, scheduler_profile). This prevents accidental “same case different name” drift.
- Aggregator includes simple sanity checks: required fields present, sample count >= min_samples, and metric units.

Out of scope:
- Driver/CUDA pinning and clock locking: pr-851
- Perf-canary integration: handled in perf-canary repo
- Eval/quality scoring: handled in eval-harness

Checklist:
- [x] Runner supports H100 + A100 pools
- [x] Aggregator outputs CSV + Parquet with stable schema
- [x] Upload script writes a manifest.jsonl linking output files + run metadata
- [x] Docs: README + example configs
- [x] CI: unit tests for case_id stability + schema validation

Rollout plan:
- Use for calibration runs first (2 models x 2 workloads x 2 GPUs)
- Then run ENG-7428 full matrix and upload to Drive (matrix-v1 sheet can import CSV)

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-7428 (execution), ENG-7422 (harness updates)
- Related: runtime pr-19880 (artifact metadata), benchmark-lab pr-851 (pinning/clock locking)
- Sprint plan: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint

review_conversation:
Grace Kim: Can we ensure case_id doesn’t change if we reorder keys in the config? We need to diff baseline vs FP8/INT8 without churn. Isabella Rossi: Yep—case_id now uses a canonical JSON dump with sorted keys + explicit field allowlist. Added test_case_id_stability.py covering key reorder + whitespace changes.

Claire Dubois: Aggregator should fail loudly if units are mixed (e.g., ttft seconds vs ms). Also please include min_samples and warmup in the metadata. Isabella Rossi: Added schema assertions for *_ms fields and included min_samples, warmup_reqs in runner.json and surfaced them into results.* columns.

Irene Choi: Pool config should default to safe resource requests to avoid starving shared nodes. Also, can you cap inflight per pool? Isabella Rossi: Added --max-inflight-per-pool (default 8) and pool YAML now includes conservative defaults. Added doc note about not using dedicated customer pools.

Allison Grant: For dashboards later we’ll want model_id/gpu_sku/quant_mode tags consistently. Please make the column names match the runtime metrics tagging conventions. Isabella Rossi: Renamed columns to model_id, gpu_sku, quant_mode, kernel_profile, scheduler_profile to align with the planned metric tags.

Rina Kobayashi: Looks good. One nit: manifest should include SHA256 so we can verify Drive downloads. Isabella Rossi: Added sha256 per file to manifest.jsonl.

Approvals: Rina approved after changes; Grace approved; Claire approved with follow-up comment to keep schema versioned (added schema_version column).
ci_summary: CI: pass. Checks: lint (py) ✅, unit tests ✅, schema validation ✅, packaging ✅. One flaky test on first run (Drive uploader mock timing) rerun passed; updated mock to be deterministic.
